assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a general enabling method that reshaped how amines are coupled to arenes, with huge impact on pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and materials. It is clear, original and demonstrably used everywhere; it complements the 2010 cross-coupling prize rather than duplicating it.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled, broadly applicable catalytic systems; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor, so a two-person prize is the cleanest fit, with Kosugi's priority a possible argument for a third.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of confirmation, industrial scale use and mechanistic understanding; recognition is fully mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: How the committee weighs the Kosugi/Migita precursor work against the later general catalysts.
Whether the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize is judged to have already covered this area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silica opened a new class of porous solids with tunable 2-10 nm pores and became a platform for catalysis, adsorption, nanocasting and hierarchical materials. It is a field I know closely, and the structure proofs (TEM, diffraction, later electron crystallography) are convincing and original.
assessment.attribution: Mobil's M41S/MCM-41 (Kresge, Beck) is the foundational discovery, with FSM-16 (Inagaki) as parallel work; Ryoo (ordered carbons, MCM-48 and SBA-15 era chemistry) and Zhao/Stucky (SBA-15 with large pores) broadened it. Credit is spread over six names and the choice of three is contestable; priority between Mobil and Japanese groups needs care.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of confirmation and heavy use; scientifically mature. Industrial impact is more modest than for zeolites, which could temper the case.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit among the Mobil, Japanese and later SBA/KIT groups.
Whether application impact is sufficient given limited industrial adoption of mesoporous silica.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts (new frameworks, organic structure-directing agents, active-site engineering, shape selectivity) underlies refining, petrochemicals and emission control. The link from structure to function is exactly the kind that rigorous crystallographic evidence supports.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalytic design and industrial transfer), Davis (framework and chiral/extra-large-pore synthesis, Beta/active-site work) and Zones (SSZ materials at Chevron with OSDAs) are the most defensible trio; Yu and Tsapatsis are strong but would crowd the prize. The field's credit is broad and the boundary with the older zeolite literature is blurred.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and large-scale industrial use; mature. The risk is that the discovery is a field rather than a single crisp invention.
uncertainties: Whether this can be framed as one discovery rather than a broad body of work.
Credit boundaries with historic zeolite pioneers outside the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation via PROTACs and molecular glues created a new therapeutic modality, with several compounds in clinical trials and mechanistic insight from ternary-complex structures. Conceptually original, with clear chemistry at the core.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies/Sakamoto introduced the PROTAC concept; Ciulli made the VHL ligands and structural foundations. Handa/Ito (cereblon as thalidomide target) and Gray add significant claims to the molecular-glue half, so the compound discovery needs different recognition for its parts.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still unfolding; confirmation of the concept is strong but no approved PROTAC drug yet, so timing may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Allocation between PROTAC and molecular-glue/cereblon lines.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached silicon-competitive solar efficiencies in about a decade and spawned a major materials class. The structure-property relationships are well established by diffraction and spectroscopy, and the impact on energy research is large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka (first perovskite-sensitised cell), Park (solid-state ~10% device) and Snaith (thin-film planar and efficiency breakthrough) cover the early decisive steps; Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also have substantial claims, so any trio leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Very strong early confirmation of efficiency, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercialisation remain unresolved, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Device stability and scale-up are unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at XFELs gives room-temperature, damage-free structures from microcrystals and time-resolved views of reactions. It is an enabling structural method in the same spirit as the nanocrystal diffraction techniques I work on, extending crystallography to crystals too small for conventional synchrotron use.
assessment.attribution: Chapman, Fromme and Hajdu are tied to the founding 2011 experiments and the underlying concept; Schlichting led important time-resolved work. The credit among the four is plausible but needs a closer look at the original proposal versus the first demonstration.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across several XFELs, though routine access is limited; time-resolved applications are still maturing.
uncertainties: Priority between the concept (Hajdu, Chapman) and the first protein demonstration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks, using engineered deaminases fused to Cas proteins; it is chemical protein and nucleotide engineering with immediate therapeutic relevance, and clinical trials are underway.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the design of both cytosine and adenine base editors (Komor, Gaudelli as lead authors); Nishida/Kondo contributed an independent cytidine-deaminase approach. A solo or Liu-led prize is the cleanest, but trainees' roles are significant.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed by many groups; clinical evidence is emerging but not yet established, so it may be somewhat early. The 2020 CRISPR prize also lowers the novelty threshold for committee members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional and isotope-labelled solution NMR, TROSY-based methods and relaxation dispersion allow structure and dynamics of large biomolecules to be studied; this is a core structural technique with decades of impact. Its main limit is that Wüthrich's 2002 prize already recognised NMR structure determination.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay were central to triple-resonance and isotopic-labelling methods, residual dipolar couplings, and dynamics; Wagner and Palmer also contributed. Credit is broad and the boundary with the Wüthrich prize must be justified.
assessment.maturity: Mature and extensively confirmed; timing is not a concern, but novelty relative to the earlier NMR prizes is.
uncertainties: Whether the prize is seen as redundant with the 2002 NMR prize.
